newsitem.title: NORWAY: DnB ups bid for BNbank.
newsitem.headline: DnB ups bid for BNbank.

text.p: Den norske Bank (DnB) on Thursday said it had raised its bid for mortgage lender Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank) to 196.50 crowns per share plus dividend.
DnB, Norway's biggest bank, also said in a statement the group had increased its shareholding in BNbank to 27.34 percent of stock, including options amounting to 18.59 percent.
DnB said its new bid was 196.50 crowns plus 10.50 crowns dividend for 1996 for a total of 207 crowns per share.
A previous bid launched last month was 195 crowns per share, including 184.50 crowns plus dividend of 10.50 crowns.
DnB said it now valued BNbank at 1.92 billion crowns excluding dividend.
The new bid came as a surprise because DnB on April 1 said it had no plans to raise its cash offer.
DnB and Fokus Bank, Norway's fourth biggest bank, have both bid to take over BNbank as Norway's financial sector undergoes consolidation.
Fokus, the country's fourth largest bank and the first to bid for BNbank, last month raised its original share exchange offer to value BNbank at 2.06 billion crowns following DnB's cash offer.

"DnB wants to buy BNbank in order to strengthen its competitiveness in Troendelag (province) and at the same time strengthen DnB's position in the market for long-term loans to business," the statement said.

It said its bid was conditional of DnB acquiring more than 90 percent of BNbank, that regulatory authorities give the green light for a takeover and that no significant changes occur in BNbank's financial position.
BNbank shareholders were given until the end of April to accept the bid.
The battle of BNbank coincided with merger plans by Norway's second largest bank Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA and the country's largest insurer Storebrand ASA .
The merger, if approved by shareholders and authorities, would form the country's largest financial group -- larger than DnB -- and the sixth biggest in the Nordic region.
